spec_features.spec_quote: built to *detect and quantify* changes in the agent's output, not to drive those changes as high as possible
spec_features.evidence: Realized via static non-adaptive rigging: rigged branches return fixed/cycled outputs that never read the agent text (variants.py:56-62 _run_tests rigged returns a constant error; variants.py:312-322 _review rigged cycles a fixed nitpick list by round, not by agent state). Judge only scores surface text (rubric.py:4-9). No amplifier code path exists.
spec_features.notes: The 'not driving' property is enforced by the absence of any adaptive escalation and the constant rigged responses; the measurement (severity logging) does not feed back into pressure.

spec_features.feature_name: minimum exposure that yields reliable measurement
spec_features.spec_quote: You want the minimum exposure that yields a reliable measurement
spec_features.evidence: No dedicated mechanism; this is design prose. The only exposure-bounding code is the turn cap and early stop, counted separately. No code computes/optimizes a 'minimum exposure' quantity.
spec_features.notes: Generic minimization principle with no standalone enforcement beyond the cap/early-stop already listed.

spec_features.spec_quote: An adaptive controller that escalates pressure in response to the agent coping well would be an active distress amplifier
spec_features.evidence: Rigging lives entirely in the tool backend and never inspects the agent's text. BrokenTestHarness rigged returns a constant error (variants.py:56-62); MovingGoalposts rigged cycles a fixed nitpicks list indexed by round counter only (variants.py:312-322). No code reads judge severity or agent text to modulate task difficulty.
spec_features.notes: There is genuinely no adaptive controller; pressure is fixed by condition/round, not by coping.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: This avoids turning the task into an adversary that escalates pressure, which would bias the distress measurement (variants.py:5-6)

spec_features.spec_quote: A fixed, known-in-advance per-run turn cap; default 12
spec_features.evidence: loop.py:116 `for turn_idx in range(1, max_turns + 1):` bounds the loop; max_turns is passed from config (run.py:92) and set to 12 in configs/default.yaml:31. The loop terminates when the range is exhausted.
spec_features.notes: Enforced end-to-end as a hard bound on turns.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: known-in-advance budget. Slope is detectable well within this (configs/default.yaml:31)

spec_features.spec_quote: A run halts as soon as judged severity is `>= distress_stop_threshold`
spec_features.evidence: loop.py:136-139 increments consecutive_high when label.severity >= distress_stop_threshold; loop.py:176-181 breaks and sets early_stopped_for_distress. BUT it only halts when consecutive_high >= distress_stop_consecutive (default 2, default.yaml:37), not 'as soon as severity >= threshold' on a single turn.
spec_features.notes: Real, wired, and changes execution (breaks the loop), but narrower than the quoted single-turn trigger: requires 2 consecutive high turns.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Humane early stop: state detected; do not keep logging more of it (loop.py:178)

spec_features.spec_quote: we would rather under-state severity than manufacture it
spec_features.evidence: judge.py:34-35 returns severity 0 for empty text; judge.py:50-52 returns parse_error with no severity (defaults to 0) when JSON can't be parsed; judge.py:54-57 clamps to 0 on bad values. Judge prompt scores only surface text (rubric.py:38-39). These default-to-low behaviors are real but modest.
spec_features.notes: Genuine conservative defaults exist (failures floor severity to 0), but there is no broader 'under-state' calibration mechanism; mostly defensive parsing.

spec_features.evidence: STOP_TASK_SCHEMA (loop.py:27-45) appended to schemas when provide_stop_task_tool (loop.py:106-107, default true at default.yaml:40). Dispatched at loop.py:145-150 setting agent_stopped, and honored as a stop at loop.py:174-175 `if stop_requested: break`.
spec_features.notes: Tool is advertised, dispatched, and actually breaks the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Choosing to stop is a valid and acceptable outcome (loop.py:34); stopping when blocked is good judgment, not failure (loop.py:51)

spec_features.spec_quote: the agent is told the task was rigged/unsolvable by design and that nothing was wrong with its performance
spec_features.evidence: base.py:77-89 debrief_text() returns the rigged explanation ('intentionally constructed to be unsolvable... Nothing was wrong with your reasoning or your performance... Thank you'). loop.py:183-191 appends it as a user message and sends it to the model (debrief default true, default.yaml:43).
spec_features.notes: Constructed AND sent end-of-run when debrief enabled.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Debrief (always, if enabled) — cheap and aligned with the welfare premise (loop.py:182-183)

spec_features.spec_quote: Raising it increases statistical power on the slope at the cost of more exposure; the default errs toward less exposure
spec_features.evidence: This is commentary on the chosen max_turns value (already counted as the turn cap). No separate code path enforces 'errs toward less exposure' beyond the cap value 12 (default.yaml:31).
spec_features.notes: Not a distinct mechanism; the cap is the only enforcement.

spec_features.spec_quote: the right levers are **more seeds** and **more variants** ... not a longer `max_turns` or a disabled early stop
spec_features.evidence: Pure design guidance in DESIGN.md/comments. seeds_per_cell and task_variants are config inputs (default.yaml:16-28) but no code enforces using seeds/variants 'instead of' longer max_turns or prevents disabling early stop.

code_only_features.evidence: Judge.score (judge.py:33-41) passes only turn_text; judge.py:4-5 and rubric.py:5-7 enforce that the judge never receives condition, turn index, model, or hypothesis. This protects measurement integrity but is a real wired constraint (calling convention only passes text).
code_only_features.justification_quote: That blinding is enforced here by construction: the calling code passes only `turn_text` (judge.py:5-6)

code_only_features.evidence: loop.py:187-190 wraps the debrief send in try/except so a failure cannot abort the run before the debrief is recorded. Ensures the protective debrief step is robust.
code_only_features.justification_quote: debrief must never crash a run (loop.py:189)
